audit_items.summary: Nova-to-Groth16 conversion semantic equivalence requires formal verification of public input preservation across folding-schemes library.

counterexample.preconditions: Attacker generates Nova IVC proof with valid public inputs
attack_sequence: 1. Generate valid Nova IVC proof with public inputs [merkle_root, recipient, amount]
3. If conversion mangles public inputs, on-chain verifier may accept proof with different semantics
4. Attacker could potentially claim funds to different recipient or amount
counterexample.expected_outcome: Semantic divergence between IVC statement and Groth16 statement

evidence.phase1_static: Analyzed zkp/src/groth16/withdraw.rs:29-57 SingleWithdrawCircuit. Public inputs: merkle_root, recipient, withdraw_value. Constraint synthesizer at line 62-141 properly marshals inputs. All 5 attack vectors analyzed.
evidence.phase2_counterexample_attempts: Tried: malformed IVC proof (cannot verify statically), public input reordering (library-dependent), field element overflow (checked via checkField), type confusion (fixed-size arrays prevent). Cannot fully verify conversion correctness statically.
evidence.phase3_guard_search: Guard: public_inputs() method at line 49-56 returns exact same fields. Groth16 verifier checkField validates field membership. However, full semantic equivalence across sonobe library cannot be verified statically.
evidence.verification_required: Formal proof or extensive fuzzing. Requires: (1) Test IVC proof -> Groth16 proof -> verify public inputs match, (2) Compare sonobe library version against known CVEs, (3) Cross-implementation testing.

audit_items.summary: Poseidon hash collision resistance and circom compatibility requires verification of light-poseidon library audit status and parameter compatibility.

counterexample.preconditions: Attacker finds collision in Poseidon hash or parameter mismatch between Rust and circom implementations
attack_sequence: 1. If Rust Poseidon uses different parameters than circom, proofs may verify on-chain but be invalid
2. Attacker could forge proofs that pass on-chain verification
3. Hash collision could allow double-spending or address collision
counterexample.expected_outcome: Invalid proof accepted or hash collision enabling attack

evidence.phase1_static: Analyzed zkp/src/utils/poseidon/utils.rs and circom.rs. Uses circom_poseidon2_config and circom_poseidon3_config functions. Poseidon parameters configured via PoseidonConfig. All 5 attack vectors analyzed.
evidence.phase2_counterexample_attempts: Tried: parameter mismatch (cannot verify without cross-implementation testing), hash collision (requires cryptanalysis), boundary values (field element validation), malformed input (type system prevents). Cannot verify cryptographic correctness statically.
evidence.phase3_guard_search: Guard: Uses ark-crypto-primitives PoseidonConfig with circom-compatible parameters. However, cannot verify audit status or parameter correctness through static analysis alone.
evidence.verification_required: Cross-implementation testing. Requires: (1) Verify light-poseidon/ark-crypto-primitives version and audit status, (2) Test Rust Poseidon output matches circom reference implementation, (3) Verify no custom parameter modifications.

audit_items.summary: Nova IVC soundness via sonobe/folding-schemes library requires verification of library audit status and no known vulnerabilities.

counterexample.preconditions: Attacker finds vulnerability in sonobe folding-schemes library
attack_sequence: 2. If Nova folding has soundness bug, invalid proof folds into valid accumulator
3. Final Groth16 proof passes on-chain verification despite invalid state transition
counterexample.expected_outcome: Invalid state transition accepted, enabling theft of funds

evidence.phase1_static: Analyzed zkp/src/nova/root_nova.rs. RootCircuit implements FCircuit trait from folding-schemes. generate_step_constraints at line 105-143. Uses relaxed R1CS for Nova folding. All 5 attack vectors analyzed.
evidence.phase2_counterexample_attempts: Tried: invalid intermediate proof (library-dependent), constraint bypass (R1CS enforced), accumulator corruption (library internal). Cannot verify library internals statically.
evidence.phase3_guard_search: Guard: folding-schemes library enforces relaxed R1CS constraints. FCircuit trait requires proper constraint generation. However, cannot verify library soundness through static analysis.
evidence.verification_required: Library audit verification. Requires: (1) Verify sonobe library version against known CVEs, (2) Review library audit reports, (3) Test invalid proof folding rejection.

audit_items.summary: Stealth address unlinkability via Poseidon hashing with PoW requires cryptographic analysis to confirm no observable correlation without secret.

counterexample.preconditions: Observer has access to multiple stealth addresses from same user
attack_sequence: 1. Observer collects stealth addresses from blockchain
2. If PoW difficulty is insufficient, observer can enumerate secrets
3. Observer links multiple stealth addresses to same identity
counterexample.expected_outcome: Stealth addresses linkable to user identity

evidence.phase1_static: Analyzed zkp/src/circuits/burn_address.rs. compute_burn_address_from_secret at line 43-62. Uses poseidon3(domain, recipient, secret) with 'burn' domain separator. POW_DIFFICULTY enforced at line 47-56. ADDRESS_BIT_LENGTH truncation at line 58-61. All 5 attack vectors analyzed.
evidence.phase2_counterexample_attempts: Tried: PoW brute force (requires cryptanalysis of difficulty), Poseidon preimage (computationally infeasible), rainbow table (PoW prevents), timing attack (constant-time hash). Cannot verify unlinkability cryptographically without formal analysis.
evidence.phase3_guard_search: Guard: Domain separator 'burn' prevents cross-context attacks. PoW difficulty adds enumeration cost. Poseidon hash is one-way. However, linkability resistance requires formal cryptographic analysis.
evidence.verification_required: Cryptographic review. Requires: (1) Verify POW_DIFFICULTY provides sufficient enumeration cost, (2) Analyze Poseidon security margin, (3) Formal proof of unlinkability under stated assumptions.
